content.title: Texas vs. BYU Prediction on Spread for NCAA Tournament – 3/19/26
content.text: It’s an SEC vs. Big 12 clash in the first round of the 2026 NCAA Tournament, as the Texas Longhorns attempt to upset the 1.5-point favorite BYU Cougars at 7:25 p.m. ET on TBS. With the Longhorns sliding a bit and the Cougars having cooled off after a lava-hot start to the season, neither side carries a ton of momentum into Thursday. That said, both sides have everything to play for to stay alive this week. Below, we’ll break down our Texas vs. BYU prediction on spread for Thursday’s game. Since that point, the Longhorns are just 5-5, including four losses of 10 or more points. Despite that, head coach Sean Miller’s crew took down NC State in a 68-66 thriller to move on to the field of 64 teams. Now playing with house money to an extent, Texas attempts to show it’s here to stay.Find our favorite NCAA Tournament Upset picks for Thursday NightAt one stage of this terrific college basketball season, head coach Kevin Young’s BYU crew was 17-2 and looked destined to make a deep tourney run. Since then, however, the Cougars have gone 6-9 and don’t look like the same team anymore.Nonetheless, BYU has managed to rip off three wins in its last four opportunities and has one of the nation’s best players in projected top 2026 NBA Draft pick, F AJ Dybantsa. Dating back to 1949, this is the eighth time Texas and BYU will meet up in a game. The Cougars own a commanding 5-2 series lead but the scoring differential is all knotted up. According to KenPom, the Cougars are 20th in net rating at +25.17. The Longhorns sit 37th at +19.12.Both offenses are potent, as BYU ranks 16th with a 124.7 adjusted offensive efficiency while Texas is 23rd at 123.2.What could separate these programs is the turnover battle. Both sides are in the top 100 at protecting the rock on offense but, per Bart Torvik, the Longhorns are 348th on defense with a measly 13.3% turnover clip. The midrange battle in this one could get ugly. Per CBB Shot Charts, both defenses allow 38.4% or worse on short midrange looks and 35.9% or worse on long midrange ones. Dybantsa is playing some of his best basketball at the perfect time. The true freshman forward is averaging 27.0 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 4.1 assists over his last 10 games.
